phrag_cost.why: Two official figures disagree by an order of magnitude. DWR GSL Basin Integrated Plan, M&I Water Conservation (Aug 2025), p.81-82: treatment $1,270-$2,540/acre, savings 17,000-57,000 ac-ft/yr, 'estimated cost between $610 and $4,050 per ac-ft' (documented analysis). 2026 legislative interim slide (le.utah.gov 00000790): '$500/acre, cost=$60 million' for 300 KAF/yr = $200/AF (summary figure). Value set to the low end of the documented estimate; range spans both.

mi_reference_price.why: Re-opened JVWCD 2026/2027 Adopted Water Rates Summary: 15 member wholesale rates $474.11-$811.41/AF, median $639.92 (re-sorted and checked). $380 is below every rate. High end is SLC retail at ~$2,173/AF (21 ccf average).

crop_cost.why: Ag Water Optimization report Table B-10: crop substitution $276 (winter wheat), $424 (corn), $493 (spring wheat) per AF; value 318.4 lies inside.

application_cv.why: NASS IWMS 2023 Table 10 Utah: between-farm-class CV 0.29 is a lower bound on field CV.

phrag_lag.why: FFSL via UPR 2026-04-16: 'three to five years to remove any given patch'.

phrag_cap.why: DWR Aug 2025 M&I report p.81: 'between 17,000 and 57,000 additional ac-ft of water per year' (DWQ 2017).

goal_added.why: Strike Team Mar 2026 summary p.29: 'Additional 800 KAF/year ... the additional inflow needed to fill Great Salt Lake to the minimum healthy lake level (4,198 feet) by 2055.' Same 1,665 KAF/yr baseline the model uses; 875 appears in no source.

application_mean.why: NASS 2023 IWMS Table 39, Utah alfalfa: 523,658 irrigated acres, 2.4 average acre-feet applied (pressure 2.6, gravity 2.0); all other hay also 2.4.

irrigation_net_value.why: GSL-BIP Ag Water Optimization report (2026) Table B-8: full-season alfalfa, 1.50 AF/acre depletion savings, WTA $236 per AF; Table B-7 $355/acre. The charge is levied on depletion, so the per-AF-depleted figure applies; 133 = $355/2.64 per AF applied.

ramp_years.why: Ag Water Optimization report assumes irrigation upgrades roll out over 10 years.

growth_draw_2055.why: No source projects 92 KAF/yr. Strike Team 2025 p.13: M&I depletion 'have not changed substantially since 1989', 325 KAF in 2023. Keep value, mark as assumption.

urban_to_lake.why: No source states a share; DWR turf figures bound it above at ~0.44 (depletion saved / water saved).

hay_net_return.why: Ag Water Optimization report Table B-7 WTA $355/acre includes 'A flat $50 per acre ... for additional leasing-related costs' (p.B-5), so forgone return = $305/acre; rebuilt from yield x $212/ton less operating cost, acreage-weighted = $304.5.

landscape_sqft.why: DWR Regional Water Conservation Goals (2019) Table 4-9, 2015 average landscaped area per lot, population-weighted over the 11 GSL-basin counties = 5,785 sq ft. The model's 5,154 / 8,868 appear nowhere in the report.

turf_need.why: Jackson & Mohadjer (2003, Irrigation Association): Salt Lake City turf net ET 'near 24 inches of water per season'. Display-only coefficient.

phrag_delivery.why: Neither cited source gives a delivery share; Strike Team Mar 2026 p.12: 'Additional research is needed to quantify water savings from phragmites treatment'.

onfarm_cap.why: Ag Water Optimization report Table ES-1/5-2: Utah sprinkler upgrades 16 KAF under $210/AF, 37 KAF under $510/AF; whole-basin irrigation-only strategy 132.6 KAF at $563/AF.

retire_capacity.why: GSL Watershed Enhancement Trust 2025 Impact Report: permanent transactions ~21 KAF/yr (diversion basis), 2023-25.

compliance_floor.why: Finley & Basu (2020, WRR) via Univ. of Waterloo release: restrictions 'had surprisingly little effect on average summer water use'.

response_k.why: Strike Team Mar 2026 p.29: '+800 KAF/year results in a 2034 mean elevation of 4,196.9 feet'. Re-run in the model's own lake balance from 4,191.0 ft (1 Oct 2025): k=0.17 gives 4,196.87 ft in 2034; k=0.12 gives 4,195.93 (1 ft slow).

lease_capacity.why: GSL Watershed Enhancement Trust 2025 Impact Report: 'voluntary water transactions in 2025 were nearly 72,500 acre-feet' (64,000/69,190/72,485 AF 2023-25), objective 100,000 AF/yr; Ag Water Optimization report's 10% leasing scenario (132 KAF basin-wide) described as 'herculean'. High of 1,600 had no support.

lake_value_per_af.why: No cited source states $2,440/AF. It reproduces as ECONorthwest (2019) cost of decline $1.69-2.17B/yr (midpoint $1.93B) / ~790-800 KAF/yr needed added inflow = ~$2,440/AF. Numerator is largely gross output (mineral extraction), not net welfare, in 2019 dollars. Only published per-AF figure: NBER w35270 (2026) $600-1,800/AF for dust-health benefits alone. Keep value, label derived with formula, widen low to 600. ECONorthwest PDF and NBER paper were bot-blocked; quoted via Audubon summary and Utah Business press release.

streamflow_decline_2055.why: Strike reports give no quantitative future streamflow decline; a 2013 study of Salt Lake City watersheds (1.8-6.5% less flow per degree F, via UCAR) makes 100 KAF/yr plausible but does not state it.

baseline_inflow.why: Strike Team Mar 2026: '2000-2025 ... inflows averaged 1,665 KAF/year'.

evap_gross.why: USGS OFR 78-912 p.12: '2.9 million acre-ft ... equivalent to about 45 in. per year'; Mohammed & Tarboton 2012 1.14 m. Caveat: evap_gross, precip_lake and inflow_efficiency are collinear (only (evap-precip)/efficiency is pinned by the USU calibration), so sweeping evap_gross alone overstates its tornado swing. DWR 2,733 KAF/yr evaporation implies ~35 in/yr at today's smaller area.

shepherd_start.why: Strike Team Mar 2026 Fig 2: 149,277 AF (2024), 163,468 AF (2025 prelim) dedicated and delivered. Caveat: much is in-lake mineral-extraction water; river-delivered dedications are ~70-135 KAF.

lake_now.why: Re-fetched USGS NWIS daily values, site 10010000 (Saltair), parameter 62614: 2025-09-30 4191.1 (approved) = the model's old value; 2026-09-30 4189.7 (provisional), 2026-10-18 4189.8. The plan starts in 2027, so the end of water year 2026 is the right starting level. Note: this is below serious_low (4,190).

inflow_cv.why: Research agent summed USGS daily flows for the Bear, Weber and Jordan gauges into water-year totals: CV 0.55 (1989-2025), 0.50 (2000-2025), 0.60 (1950-2025). Not independently recomputed by the reviewer; re-run before relying on it.

mi_depletion.why: Agent finds 328 appears in no source and proposes ~354 (2020-24 Strike table: 640 M&I - 421.6 residential + 136 minerals). Changing it means restructuring CONSUMERS (which must sum to 2,387) and charge_base together; do it with the tables batch. Minerals there is 152 vs 136 in the current table.

charge_base.why: Defined as ag_depletion + mi_depletion; follows mi_depletion (agent proposes ~1,938).

serious_low.why: 4,190 is the Strategic Plan's contingency floor (p.26); the plan and Strike Team place 'serious adverse effects' below 4,192 ft. Relabel or switch to 4,192 depending on what the label should mean.

lease_base_rate.why: Ag Water Optimization report 2026, Sec 5.1 / Table B-8: full-season alfalfa lease $236 per AF; Gardner Institute water banking brief (Feb 2023): 'cost per acre-foot may range between $150 and $300'. 380 matches Colorado River programmes, not the GSL basin.

state_interest.why: Utah Treasurer 2025 Debt Affordability Study: 'average rate of 1.82% on outstanding GO debt' with 'higher long-term interest rates' now; PTIF earnings ~4.0% (Dec 2025). 3% is a judgement between them, labelled assumption.

lake_jobs_full.why: le.utah.gov interim 2022 00004675 slide 'Estimated Total Economic Impact' (Bioeconomics 2012, 2010 data): TOTAL ALL SECTORS 7,706 (direct+indirect+induced); direct 3,557. No source found for 8,650.

livestock_jobs_at_risk.why: No cited source has 1,900; BLS QCEW 2024: cattle and dairy wage jobs ~1,670 statewide, ~1,000 in basin counties (self-employed not counted).

hay_value_per_af.why: NASS 2025 Utah alfalfa ~$748/acre; / ~3 ft consumed = 245 (model); / 1.5 AF/acre fallowing saving (state 2026 study) = ~$500.

capital_price.why: Cedar City paid ~$12,100/AF in 2023 (Western Water); capitalised Utah lease rates give ~$3,000-8,300/AF. The ~$208/AF figure was a bankruptcy purchase of mineral brine rights plus a plant.

mandate_pull.why: SCPP grew 64 -> 109 projects, 38,000 -> 64,000 AF (KJZZ syndication of Aspen Journalism), but credited to a fixed price, not a mandate threat.

pref_incentives.why: 0.58 confirmed in the March 2026 Deseret News/Hinckley poll (800 voters), not noble_2026.

pref_penalties.why: 0.22 confirmed in the March 2026 Deseret News/Hinckley poll, not noble_2026.

farmer_compensation_low.why: $29/resident x 3.4M from the Oregon State study (Environmental Challenges, 2025); cite it directly. Still used nowhere in the model.

farmer_compensation_high.why: $124/resident x 3.4M, same Oregon State study. Still used nowhere in the model.

hay_acres.why: 2022 Census of Agriculture irrigated hay land, 12 Utah basin counties (Wasatch withheld, ~8,000 estimated). 399,500 only fits with Idaho and Wyoming, which a Utah levy cannot reach. Recompute county sum before applying.

hay_depletion.why: 2019-23 Hay/Turf depletion read from Fig 2-5 of the 2026 Ag Optimization report (+/-20 KAF, whole basin; Utah-only ~540). 1,055 = 399,500 acres x 2.64 = water applied. Used nowhere in the model; tie it to CONSUMERS or delete.

lawn_water.why: 108 gpcd residential outdoor (2015) x 3.07M basin residents; DWR counts it as delivered water. Apply together with the lawn cluster (basin_lawns, landscape_sqft, people_per_home, share_in_basin) and re-check the lawn_inches reconciliation.

people_per_home.why: Gardner Institute 2025 household size 'nearly 3.0'; 2.83 looks like a 2030s projection.

share_in_basin.why: 2025 population estimates for the 12 basin counties / state.

basin_lawns.why: 1.2M x 0.86 x 0.72 = 743k; the old household size and basin share errors cancelled. Agent also resolves findings.md lawn mismatch: Table 4-9 area is per residential unit, so multiply by all ~1.02M basin households; see results/b7.json.

herd_feed_surplus.why: Not in NASS; published export estimates 6-20% of Utah's ~2.5M tons = 150k-520k tons.

industrial_pipeline_water.why: Cited sources hold no project volumes; only ~1.2 KAF traced (Stratos data center 1,215 AF diverted; Tooele nuclear campus ~15,000 gal/day). Display only.

industrial_pipeline_jobs.why: Not in the cited DWS page; state nuclear campus booklet estimates 5,000-10,000 permanent jobs, contingent on federal selection. Display only.
